text.p: Bangladesh and India allowed an outdated 25-year friendship treaty to expire on Tuesday, Bangladesh officials said.
Both sides agreed not to extend the treaty, signed in 1972 by then Bangladesh President Sheikh Mujibur Rahman and Indian Prime Minister Indira Gandhi.

Mujib's daughter Sheikh Hasina, now Bangladesh Prime Minister, has called the treaty "useless" given the two countries' membership in the seven-member South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC).

"After formation of the SAARC which is a bigger and stronger forum for economic and political cooperation, a separate Indo-Bangladesh treaty is no longer a necessity," she said during her poll campaign.
Indian diplomats were not available for comment.
The treaty specified that neither country would take part in a military alliance against the other.
It also said that "in case either party is attacked or threatened with attack, they shall immediately enter into mutual consultation in order to take appropriate measures to eliminate the threat".
India helped Bangladesh to win independence in 1971 by sending troops into then East Pakistan and sheltered one million refugees from East Pakistan through the nine months of war.
Hasina's foes have called the treaty a "deal of slavery."
